items.summary: ~6 single-line JSDoc comments restate function names without adding insight

evidence: normalizer.ts:105 '* Normalizes header to array format.' on function normalizeHeader — name is self-documenting
validator.ts:152 '* Validates a single label configuration.' on function validateLabel(label, name, context)
ruleset-validator.ts:82 '* Validates a single ruleset rule.' on function validateRule(rule, context)
ruleset-validator.ts:203 '* Validates a single ruleset.' on function validateRuleset(...)
retry-utils.ts:113 '* Checks if an error matches known transient patterns.' on function isTransientError
git-ops.ts:191-193 'Uses the same this.exec() pattern as other methods in this class' — implementation detail unhelpful to callers
detail.suggestion: Remove these one-line JSDoc comments that restate the function name. The function names are self-documenting. For git-ops.ts getChangedFiles, remove the 'Uses the same this.exec() pattern' line as it describes implementation, not behavior.

items.summary: IRepoSettingsStrategy uses verb-prefixed names while sibling strategies use bare CRUD verbs

evidence: IRulesetStrategy and ILabelsStrategy use bare CRUD: list(), get(), create(), update(), delete(). IRepoSettingsStrategy uses getSettings(), updateSettings(), setVulnerabilityAlerts(), setAutomatedSecurityFixes(), setPrivateVulnerabilityReporting() - mixing get/set prefix style with the domain noun baked into every method name.
detail.suggestion: This is low-impact given the different domain shapes (repo settings has separate security endpoints unlike labels/rulesets which are pure CRUD). If aligning, rename getSettings to get and updateSettings to update to match the sibling strategy pattern. The set* methods are unique to this strategy and justified by the separate API endpoints they call.

items.summary: parseManifestContent silently returns null for V1 manifests without logging, unlike loadManifest

evidence: loadManifest handles V1 explicitly with a comment '// V1 manifest - treat as no manifest (will be overwritten with v4)' and returns null. parseManifestContent delegates to migrateToV4 which returns null for V1 with no logging, creating an inconsistent contract between the two public entry points for manifest parsing.
detail.suggestion: Add V1 detection in parseManifestContent after migrateToV4 returns null: if isV1Manifest(parsed), log a debug message about V1 being unsupported before returning null. This aligns the contract with loadManifest's explicit handling.

items.summary: authenticated-git-ops.test.ts uses it() instead of the codebase-wide test() convention

evidence: This is the only file out of ~93 test files that imports and uses 'it' from 'node:test' — all others use 'test'
detail.suggestion: Replace 'import { describe, it } from "node:test"' with 'import { describe, test } from "node:test"' and change all it() calls to test() calls in this file.

items.summary: 11 test files use non-strict assert import instead of the dominant strict pattern

evidence: 11 files use 'import assert from "node:assert"' while 82 other test files use 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"'
detail.suggestion: Change all 11 files to use 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"' to match the dominant convention. This is a mechanical find-and-replace.

items.summary: 8 files bypass config/index.ts barrel for types that are re-exported from it

evidence: sync/types.ts imports FileContent and RepoConfig from '../config/types.js' instead of '../config/index.js'
sync/sync-workflow.ts and sync/file-sync-strategy.ts import RepoConfig from '../config/types.js'
lifecycle/types.ts, lifecycle/repo-lifecycle-manager.ts, lifecycle/lifecycle-helpers.ts import RepoConfig/GitHubRepoSettings from '../config/types.js'
cli/sync-command.ts line 84 imports Config from '../config/types.js' despite using config/index.js elsewhere in the same file
settings/labels/converter.ts, diff.ts, formatter.ts import Label from '../../config/types.js' while sibling settings modules use the barrel
detail.suggestion: Update all 11 files to import from '../config/index.js' (or '../../config/index.js' for settings/labels/) instead of '../config/types.js'. For FileContent and ContentValue, first add them to config/index.ts type re-exports, then update sync/file-writer.ts and sync/types.ts.

items.summary: FileContent and ContentValue types consumed cross-module but not exported from config/index.ts barrel

evidence: sync/file-writer.ts imports FileContent and ContentValue from '../config/types.js' directly because config/index.ts does not re-export them
sync/types.ts imports FileContent from '../config/types.js' for the same reason
All other cross-module types (RepoConfig, Config, Label, etc.) are properly re-exported from config/index.ts
detail.suggestion: Add FileContent and ContentValue to the type re-exports in src/config/index.ts, then update sync/file-writer.ts and sync/types.ts to import from '../config/index.js'.

items.summary: runAndCollect uses Object.assign with dynamic key bypassing typed assignment

evidence: Line 267: Object.assign(entry, { [resultKey]: result }) where resultKey is 'rulesetResult' | 'labelsResult' | 'settingsResult'. ProcessorResults has these as typed optional fields, so direct assignment entry[resultKey] = result would be type-safe and more direct.
detail.suggestion: Replace Object.assign(entry, { [resultKey]: result }) with entry[resultKey] = result as ProcessorResults[typeof resultKey]. The union type on resultKey already constrains it to valid keys of ProcessorResults, making the dynamic access type-safe without Object.assign.

items.summary: wouldChange() catches all read errors as 'changed' without discriminating error codes like getFileContent()

evidence: git-ops.ts:177 catches all errors and returns true, while getFileContent() at line 150-156 discriminates ENOENT/EACCES from unexpected errors and re-throws the latter. Both methods read files in the same class but use different error handling strategies.
detail.suggestion: Apply the same ENOENT/EACCES check used in getFileContent: catch the error, check the code property, return true for expected filesystem errors, and re-throw unexpected ones. This makes the two sibling methods consistent.

items.summary: buildLifecycleReport lives in output/ while sibling buildSyncReport and buildSettingsReport live in cli/

evidence: buildLifecycleReport (output/lifecycle-report.ts:26) aggregates LifecycleAction[] into a LifecycleReport, the same data-aggregation role that buildSyncReport (cli/sync-report-builder.ts:16) and buildSettingsReport (cli/settings-report-builder.ts:33) perform for their domains
The sync and settings report-builder functions were extracted into cli/ with dedicated files, but lifecycle was not, leaving output/lifecycle-report.ts mixing data aggregation with rendering
detail.suggestion: Extract buildLifecycleReport into a new cli/lifecycle-report-builder.ts file, mirroring the pattern established by cli/sync-report-builder.ts and cli/settings-report-builder.ts. Leave the rendering functions (formatLifecycleReportCLI, formatLifecycleSummary) in output/lifecycle-report.ts. Update sync-command.ts to import from the new location.

items.summary: runAndCollect uses Object.assign with dynamic key to populate ProcessorResults, bypassing type safety

evidence: At sync-command.ts:267, Object.assign(entry, { [resultKey]: result }) dynamically assigns processor results using a string key ('rulesetResult' | 'labelsResult' | 'settingsResult'), bypassing TypeScript's structural type checking at the boundary where three different processor result types converge into ProcessorResults
detail.suggestion: Replace the generic runAndCollect with three direct calls inside buildSettingsDescriptors or applyRepoSettings. Each descriptor's run callback can directly assign to the typed field: entry.rulesetResult = result, entry.labelsResult = result, entry.settingsResult = result. This eliminates the dynamic key while keeping the descriptor pattern intact.

items.summary: processOrphans detects orphans and computes manifest but does not process (delete) them

evidence: ManifestManager.processOrphans() at line 30 returns OrphanProcessResult (manifest, existingManifest, filesToDelete) — it detects orphans and prepares deletion list but does not actually delete anything. The companion method deleteOrphans() performs the actual deletion. The name 'processOrphans' implies end-to-end processing but only covers detection.
detail.suggestion: Rename processOrphans to detectOrphans or computeOrphanPlan to distinguish it from deleteOrphans which performs the actual mutation. Update the interface IManifestManager and calling code in FileSyncOrchestrator accordingly.

items.summary: repository-processor.test.ts defines local createMockExecutor shadowing shared mock import

evidence: Line 22 imports shared mock as 'createExecutorMock' alias, then line 28 defines local 'function createMockExecutor(): ICommandExecutor' that returns a bare no-op executor
The shared createMockExecutor with {defaultResponse: ''} would produce the same result, making the local definition redundant
detail.suggestion: Remove the local createMockExecutor and use createMockExecutor({}) from test/mocks/index.js directly (it already defaults to empty string responses). Remove the alias import and use the shared name consistently.

items.summary: formatFullConfig uses double assertion 'as unknown as Record<string, unknown>' on Ruleset

evidence: Line 292: ruleset as unknown as Record<string, unknown> -- Ruleset is a well-typed interface with known keys (target, enforcement, bypassActors, conditions, rules). The double assertion through unknown bypasses all type checking.
detail.suggestion: Use Object.entries on the Ruleset directly since renderNestedObject only needs key-value iteration. Alternatively, widen the renderNestedObject parameter to accept Record<string, unknown> | Ruleset and handle the iteration internally, avoiding the double cast.

items.summary: file-sync-strategy.ts narrows FileAction via as-cast after filter instead of type predicate

evidence: Line 43: f.action as 'create' | 'update' | 'delete' after .filter((f) => f.action !== 'skip') -- the compiler still sees the full FileAction union after filter, so the cast is unchecked
detail.suggestion: Add a type predicate: function isActiveAction(f: FileAction): f is FileAction & { action: 'create' | 'update' | 'delete' } { return f.action !== 'skip'; } and use .filter(isActiveAction) to let the compiler verify the narrowing without a cast.

items.summary: Repo settings processor reduces changes to Record<string, unknown> then casts to GitHubRepoSettings

evidence: Lines 116-124: .reduce() accumulates into {} as Record<string, unknown>, then the result is cast as GitHubRepoSettings. The accumulator type erases all property-level checking during the reduce loop.
detail.suggestion: Type the accumulator as Partial<GitHubRepoSettings> instead of Record<string, unknown>. Since change.property is already typed as keyof GitHubRepoSettings, the assignment acc[change.property] = change.newValue would be compile-time checked against the property types.
